newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA TO SEEK BALANCE OF PAYMENT SUPPORT FROM EU.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA TO SEEK BALANCE OF PAYMENT SUPPORT FROM EU.

text.p: Crisis-torn Bulgaria will seek balance of payment support from the European Union (EU) needed to repay debts and for vital imports like grain and fuel, foreign minister Stoyan Stalev said on Wednesday.
In a meeting with EU officials planned for later this month to discuss association issues, Bulgaria will stress its current problems caused by the crisis, Stalev told a news conference.
"The talks will focus mostly on seeking balance of payment support and presenting privatisation opportunities," said Stalev.

The interim cabinet, appointed a week ago, inherited from the former Socialist administration paralysing fuel shortages, galloping prices, bread queues, a sinking national currency, stagnant industry and enormous debts.
The Socialists bowed to 30 days of mass protests agreeing last week to hold elections on April 19, almost two years before the end of their term.

Finance Minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said last week Bulgaria hoped to receive between $300 million and $400 million from the EU. He said he believed that some $200 million dues to the EU and $126 million to the Paris Club of official creditors could be repaid only by new EU loans.
One third of one billion dollar pending foreign debt payments this year is due in the first quarter, coinciding with the term of the interim cabinet.
"We must clearly state that Bulgaria is unswervingly committed to market economy policies...Bulgaria needs big privatisation deals," said Stalev.

In a bid to raise revenue, the interim cabinet said it will offer for sale a stake in Bulgaria's biggest refinery Neftochim and decided to put up for sale a bigger than earlier planned stake in the Bulgarian Telecommunications Company.
Bulgaria also hopes to win funding from the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund, missions from which are due in Sofia in the next few days.
Stalev said the foreign policy priorities of the interim cabinet will focus on integrating the country with the EU and bringing financial stabilisation to the economy.
On Monday the government approved a declaration stating a clear desire to join NATO.
Bulgaria, an associate EU member since 1994, has formally applied for membership in 1995. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
